ogch.BaseSchema.tappDefinition.title: Technique-Aligned Protocol Profile (TAPP) Definition v3
ogch.BaseSchema.tappDefinition.description: A registered Technique-Aligned Protocol Profile (TAPP) definition modeled as a PLAN — prov:Plan / bios:LabProtocol (also cdi:Activity + schema:Action for the DDI-CDI process/action description). It is a reusable procedure that prescribes an analysis; the analysis OCCURRENCE is the prov:Activity in adaProduct.prov:wasGeneratedBy, which references this plan via prov:used. Because the TAPP is a plan, its instrument / bios:computationalTool / bios:reagent are directly-specified resources (not prov:used entities). The TAPP identity (name, technique, instrument, location) lives at the top level. The standard workflow is encoded in schema:actionProcess as a schema:HowTo containing an ordered sequence of cdi:Activity + schema:Action steps (sample preparation, calibration, acquisition, data processing, quality control). Each workflow step carries its own parameters, reagents, and instruments. TAPP-level parameters that apply across all steps remain at the top level in schema:additionalProperty. Integrates Bioschemas vocabulary for computational tools and reagents, DDI-CDI for activity sequence, and dqv:hasQualityMeasurement for quality metrics.

@context.description: JSON-LD context declaring the namespace prefixes used in a method definition. Required for the document to be a valid JSON-LD instance. Bound prefixes must include schema (always), cdi (DDI-CDI), and ada (ADA vocabulary). Additional prefixes (bios, dqv, prov, skos) are recommended when those vocabularies are used in the body of the definition.

@id.description: Persistent URI for this TAPP definition in the registry.

@type.description: Must include prov:Plan, cdi:Activity, schema:Action, ada:TAPPDefinition, and bios:LabProtocol. The TAPP is a PLAN (prov:Plan / bios:LabProtocol) — a reusable procedure description that prescribes the analysis, NOT the analysis occurrence (that is the prov:Activity in adaProduct.prov:wasGeneratedBy, which references this plan via prov:used). As a plan, its instrument / bios:computationalTool / bios:reagent are directly-specified resources (bios:LabProtocol convention), not prov:used entities.

schema:name.title: Method Name
schema:name.description: Short descriptive name with version (e.g. "JEOL-8530F WDS Major Element Glass v2.1").

schema:identifier.description: DOI or other persistent ID for this method definition.

schema:description.description: Human-readable summary of the method, may be auto-generated from constant parameters at registration time.

schema:datePublished.title: Method Start Date
schema:datePublished.description: ISO 8601 date when this method configuration was first used.

schema:dateModified.description: ISO 8601 date of last update to this definition.

schema:additionalType.description: Further classification of the activity type (e.g. schema:CreateAction for a production method). A CURIE may also be written as a JSON-LD IRI reference, which is what CDIF's schemaorgProperties/additionalProperty SHACL asks for. This was the last of the eight sites in #77 still rejecting the @id form -- with it widened, the conversion probe goes from 344/345 to 345/345.

schema:measurementTechnique.title: Technique
schema:measurementTechnique.description: The analytical technique this method implements. Must be a DefinedTerm from a controlled vocabulary of techniques.

schema:object.description: Target material(s) this method is designed to analyse (e.g. silicate glass, olivine, spinel), modeled as DefinedTerm(s) or free text; and/or the sample(s) analysed, modeled as iSamples material-sample objects (the "Samples analyzed" shape carried over from geochemProduct).

schema:name.description: Sample name/identifier as used in the lab.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Per-sample PropertyValue entries (e.g. analysis location); technique profiles constrain these.

schema:instrument.description: Instrument specification(s) for this method: a single instrument object, or an array of instruments when the method uses more than one (e.g. LA-ICP-MS = a laser ablation system plus the ICP-MS). Use schema:hasPart for instrument sub-components (spectrometers, detectors, ICP source, sample introduction system). Path-driven technique overlays select a specific instrument by schema:additionalType and constrain its sub-component tree.

bios:computationalTool.description: Software tools used for data acquisition, reduction, and processing. Each tool carries name, version, and optional URL.

bios:reagent.description: Reference materials, calibration standards, and chemical reagents used across this method. Reagents specific to a single workflow step should be placed on that step instead.

schema:location.title: Laboratory
schema:location.description: Laboratory where this method was developed. Optional; omit for methods that are instrument-generic.

schema:creator.title: Method Author
schema:creator.description:
Person or organisation who defined or is responsible for this method.
The nested schema:description is OPTIONAL, and where present it records the PROVENANCE OF THIS DEFINITION -- how the TAPP definition itself came to be, as distinct from the method it describes. It is where a definition states that it was transcribed from a published protocol, derived from existing metadata records rather than authored by the laboratory, or produced automatically and reviewed by a person. A laboratory-authored TAPP needs nothing here; a draft assembled from other sources should not be mistaken for one, so it says so. The draft TAPP sidecars target it as the 'Procedure Author Description' row.
It sits on the creator rather than at the root deliberately: the claim is about who produced the definition and how, so it belongs with that agent, and a root-level property would invite a second copy. Note that the {'@id'} branch below is sealed, so a creator given as a bare reference cannot carry it -- a reference names an agent described elsewhere and makes no claim of its own.
The property is DECLARED by the person and organization building blocks this anyOfs, where it is a plain optional string. The note is here rather than there because those two blocks are general-purpose CDIF blocks with five other consumers, and this meaning is specific to a TAPP definition.

schema:actionProcess.description: The standard workflow for this method, expressed as a schema:HowTo containing an ordered sequence of workflow steps. Each step is a cdi:Activity + schema:Action describing a distinct phase (sample preparation, calibration, acquisition, data processing, quality control). Steps carry their own parameters, reagents, instruments, and sub-steps. Exactly one step must be the sample-preparation step -- see MethodWorkflowHowTo.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Method-level Advanced-protocol parameters that apply across all workflow steps. Editable parameters are schema:PropertyValueSpecification entries (a default the analyst may override); read-only parameters are schema:PropertyValue entries carrying the fixed protocol value. Replaces the former ada:methodParameters. Technique TAPP profiles constrain the allowed entries via $refs to the parameterTemplates (specifications) and parameterValues (values) registries. Step-specific parameters should be placed on the appropriate workflow step instead.

ada:targetMaterialTemplate.description:
Template for per-target-material parameters, a target material being a material type this procedure is designed to analyse (Silicate mineral, Silicate glass, Oxide, Sulfide, Carbonate, Phosphate, Metal or alloy). Declares the target-material domain and the columns that repeat over it.
The domain is declared by the TAPP's Target Material field, marked `defines: target material`; the fields keyed BY it are the electron-beam conditions (Beam Current, Beam Mode, Beam Diameter, Beam Raster Dimensions, Beam Damage Minimization), and Primary Calibration Standard Name is keyed `target material x target species`.
Target materials are assumed present in any sample the procedure would analyse. The binding between a particular sampling unit and the material it hit is instance data, not procedure metadata, so it is recorded as a data-table column and NOT here -- this template carries only the kinds of material expected and the values that repeat over them.

ada:targetMaterialColumns.description: Columns of the per-target-material parameter table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "targetMaterial" that identifies the material named in each row.

ada:targetMaterialDeclaration.description: The material types analysed, AS THE SOURCE STATES IT. Free text on purpose, and the counterpart of ada:targetSpeciesDeclaration: a submitter may name the materials as a list, or as prose that names none individually. ada:defaultTargetMaterials carries the members that could be recognised; this carries the statement they were recognised FROM, so a cell that parses only in part loses nothing.

ada:defaultTargetMaterials.description:
The material types this procedure targets by default - the ROWS of the per-material table, and the domain `defines: target material` enumerates. An entry is a bare string or a schema:DefinedTerm naming the material, or a row object binding that material to per-material values.
A row object is keyed throughout by the schema:valueName of the columns declared in ada:targetMaterialColumns, and MUST carry the 'targetMaterial' key - the column that sibling description requires to identify the material named in each row.
Column-level constraints stay on the column: schema:readonlyValue when a value is constant across every material, and schema:defaultValue when one default serves the whole column. Use a row only for values that differ between materials.

anyOf.title: Per-target-material row
anyOf.description: One row of the per-material table, keyed by column schema:valueName. null records a value that is deliberately absent for this material rather than merely unstated.

targetMaterial.description: The material type this row is for (e.g. "Silicate mineral"), from the controlled list the TAPP's Target Material field offers, optionally qualified in the same cell. The key is the schema:valueName of the identifier column, which ada:targetMaterialColumns requires exactly one of, so a row is keyed by column valueName throughout.

ada:targetSpeciesTemplate.description: Template for per-target-species (element-specific) parameters. Defines the columns that appear in the species table, each with scope, datatype, and constraints. Target-species rows become schema:variableMeasured entries in metadata records. Typically associated with the acquisition workflow step.

ada:targetSpeciesColumns.description: Columns of the per-target-species parameter table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "targetSpecies" that identifies the analyzed constituent named in each row.

ada:targetSpeciesDeclaration.description: What this procedure analyses, AS THE SOURCE STATES IT. Free text on purpose, and the counterpart of ada:collectorConfiguration on the instrument side: submitters write the target species as a list, as a list with a sentence attached ("Mn (55Mn), Fe (57Fe) ... Pb (207Pb) in seawater"), or as prose that names no species individually at all ("Major and trace elements, masses 23-75"). ada:defaultTargetSpecies below carries the members that could be recognised; this carries the statement they were recognised FROM, so a cell that parses only in part loses nothing. Present whenever the declaration said more than the parsed rows record.

ada:defaultTargetSpecies.description:
The target species (analyzed constituents) this method targets by default — the ROWS of the per-species table. An entry is a bare string or a schema:DefinedTerm naming the species, or a row object binding that species to per-species values.
A row object is keyed throughout by the schema:valueName of the columns declared in ada:targetSpeciesColumns, and MUST carry the 'targetSpecies' key - the column that sibling description requires to identify the constituent named in each row.
Which values belong here follows the TAPP's Analysis-Level Tier. A column marked Read-Only is fixed by the procedure, so its value belongs on the row. A column marked Editable takes a starting value here that an analysis may override; the value actually used is reported per result, as a column of the data table, and surfaces as schema:variableMeasured on the data product. Values that vary per result and are not defaulted do not belong here at all.
Column-level constraints stay on the column: schema:readonlyValue when a value is constant across every target species, and schema:defaultValue when one default serves the whole column. Use a row only for values that differ between target species.

anyOf.title: Per-species row
anyOf.description: One row of the per-species table, keyed by column schema:valueName. null records a value that is deliberately absent for this species rather than merely unstated.

targetSpecies.description:
The analyzed constituent this row is for (e.g. "SiO2"). The key is the schema:valueName of the identifier column, which ada:targetSpeciesColumns requires exactly one of, so a row is keyed by column valueName throughout.
This key was 'analyte' until 2026-09-25. The rename moved the COLUMN's schema:valueName const to 'targetSpecies' but left the row half behind, so a row object could satisfy neither half: keyed 'analyte' it contradicted its own column, keyed 'targetSpecies' it failed this required. Nothing upstream caught it because every tappDefinition example lists bare strings here and so never exercises this branch; it surfaced against the 46 stored ADA method definitions, which do use row objects.

ada:monitoredPropertyTemplate.description: Template for per-monitored-property parameters, a monitored property being an instrument selection position (a mass, a Faraday cup, an energy-loss edge, an X-ray line). Declares the monitored-property domain and the columns that repeat over it. The domain is declared by different fields per technique -- Monitored Isotopes for ICP-MS, Collector Configuration for MC-ICP-MS, EELS Edges for TEM.

ada:monitoredPropertyColumns.description:
Columns of the per-monitored-property table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "monitoredProperty" identifying the selection position named in each row. ("channel" was that name before the 2026-09 rename.)
A 'collector' column is the optional one worth knowing about: it maps each monitored property to the collector that carries it. That mapping is procedure CONFIGURATION, not instrument hardware -- the same array can be wired differently by another procedure, and an analysis may override it -- which is why it belongs here on the method definition and not on schema:instrument. The collectors themselves are hardware and live there, in hasPart[Collector].ada:collectors; this column's values are their schema:name.

anyOf.title: Per-monitored-property row
anyOf.description: One row of the table, keyed by column schema:valueName.

monitoredProperty.description: The selection position measured, e.g. '⁸⁴Sr'. Becomes a schema:variableMeasured entry on the data product.

targetSpecies.description: The species this property helps determine, when it determines one. Absent for a monitor.

collector.description: schema:name of the collector carrying this property, matching an entry in schema:instrument…hasPart[Collector].ada:collectors.

ada:reportedPropertyTemplate.description: Template for the variables this procedure REPORTS and their units, as distinct from ada:targetSpeciesTemplate which records what was acquired. Declares the reported-property domain and the columns that repeat over it. It also states the procedure's scope boundary: a derived quantity inside this list is in scope, anything beyond it belongs to a separate, coupled procedure.

ada:reportedPropertyColumns.description: Columns of the reported-property table. Must include exactly one column with schema:valueName "reportedProperty" identifying the reported variable named in each row.

ada:defaultReportedProperties.description: The reported properties this procedure defines by default — the ROWS of the reported- property table. Each is a bare string or a schema:DefinedTerm identifying the property; per-property column VALUES live in the analysis record, not here.

dqv:hasQualityMeasurement.description: Quality measurements that characterize the method's expected performance (e.g. analytical precision, accuracy, counting statistics error). Uses the CDIF qualityMeasure building block.

schema:relatedLink.title: Method References
schema:relatedLink.description: Publications, Zenodo records, or other references reports describing or evaluating this method.

schema:variableMeasured.title: Reported Variables
schema:variableMeasured.description: Variables / properties this procedure reports (e.g. detection limit, limit of quantification, calibration factor, uncertainty propagation method), each modeled as a schema:PropertyValueSpecification (a procedure-level default, carrying schema:defaultValue) or a schema:PropertyValue (a measured value, carrying schema:value), keyed by schema:name. A technique profile enumerates the reported properties it defines; a dataset instance overrides each schema:defaultValue with a schema:value. Left open here — the technique overlay narrows it.

WorkflowHowTo.description: The method's standard workflow expressed as a schema:HowTo. Contains an ordered array of workflow steps in schema:step, where each step is a cdi:Activity + schema:Action.

schema:name.description: Name of the workflow (e.g. "EPMA WDS analytical workflow").

schema:url.description: URL to a published protocol document.

schema:step.description: Ordered sequence of workflow steps. Each step is a cdi:Activity + schema:Action + schema:HowToStep describing a distinct phase of the analytical procedure. This shape carries NO sample-preparation requirement, because it is used for a STEP's sub-workflow as well as for a method's top-level workflow; see MethodWorkflowHowTo for the method form that does require one.

MethodWorkflowHowTo.description:
A method's standard workflow: a WorkflowHowTo that must also include exactly one sample-preparation step (schema:name "Sample preparation" with schema:additionalType containing "bios:LabProcess"); its schema:position is left to the protocol author.
Separate from WorkflowHowTo because that shape is ALSO the sub-workflow of a single step (WorkflowStep.schema:actionProcess), and requiring sample preparation there is wrong -- a step's sub-workflow is the breakdown of that one step, so a sample-preparation step broken into mount / grind / polish / coat would have needed a nested "Sample preparation" inside itself. Both references pointed at one $def, so the method's requirement reached every sub-workflow. Nothing exercised it, as no example nests a sub-workflow.

contains.description: a sample preparation step is required.

WorkflowStep.description: A single step in the analytical workflow, modeled as a cdi:Activity + schema:Action. Each step describes a distinct phase such as sample preparation, instrument calibration, data acquisition, data processing, or quality control. Steps carry their own parameters, instruments, reagents, and may contain sub-steps via schema:actionProcess.

@type.description: All THREE are required. cdi:Activity and schema:Action carry the DDI-CDI and schema.org process semantics this model is built on; schema:HowToStep is what schema.org itself expects of a value of schema:step on a schema:HowTo, and omitting it made these steps invalid against the plain schema.org reading -- and against the base cdifProvActivity, whose own step shape requires schema:HowToStep. The two shapes disagreed, which is observable in the examples: 565 steps carried cdi:Activity + schema:Action and 15 carried schema:HowToStep, depending on which side emitted them.

schema:name.description: Name of this workflow step (e.g. "Sample preparation").

schema:description.description: Detailed description of what this step involves.

schema:position.description: Ordinal position in the workflow sequence (1-based).

schema:additionalType.description: Further classification of this step (e.g. bios:LabProcess for wet-lab steps, schema:CreateAction for production steps). A CURIE may also be written as a JSON-LD IRI reference, which is what CDIF's schemaorgProperties/additionalProperty SHACL asks for; the `contains` on the method's schema:step accepts either serialization, so widening here cannot orphan the sample-preparation requirement.

schema:instrument.description: Instrument or equipment used in this step.

bios:computationalTool.description: Software tools used in this step.

bios:reagent.description: Reference materials, standards, or reagents used in this step.

prov:used.description: Input entities consumed or referenced by this step (e.g. prepared sample from a prior step).

schema:result.description: Output entity produced by this step (can be referenced as input by a subsequent step).

schema:object.description: Reference to a prior step whose result is the input for this step (action chaining).

schema:additionalProperty.description: Step-specific parameters (e.g. beam conditions for the acquisition step, matrix correction settings for the data processing step). Editable parameters are schema:PropertyValueSpecification entries (a default the analyst may override); read-only parameters are schema:PropertyValue entries carrying the fixed protocol value.

schema:actionProcess.description: Sub-workflow for this step, expressed as a nested schema:HowTo with its own ordered steps. Use for steps that have a multi-phase internal procedure (e.g. sample preparation with mount, grind, polish, coat).

dqv:hasQualityMeasurement.description: Quality measurements specific to this workflow step.

MethodParameter.description: A parameter specification for the method, typed as schema:PropertyValueSpecification. Uses schema.org properties for value constraints (defaultValue, minValue, maxValue, readonlyValue, valueRequired) and ada: extensions for analytical method semantics (fieldScope, category, tier). Link to a controlled vocabulary via schema:inDefinedTermSet.

schema:description.description: Guidance text shown to the user in the form.

schema:propertyID.description: URI identifying this parameter type in a formal vocabulary. Links to a skos:Concept or similar term definition. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}).

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description:
Controlled vocabulary providing allowed values for this parameter. When present, form renders a dropdown/select populated from the vocabulary. Four shapes are accepted: (1) a plain URI string identifying an external SKOS ConceptScheme; (2) an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere; (3) a LabeledLink (LinkRole with name and URL); (4) an inline schema:DefinedTermSet enumerating the allowed values
    as schema:DefinedTerm objects (replaces the prior ada:enumeration).

anyOf.description: Object reference to a vocabulary defined elsewhere.
Inline schema:DefinedTermSet listing the allowed values as schema:DefinedTerm objects. Use when no external vocabulary URI is available; replaces the deprecated ada:enumeration property.

schema:defaultValue.description: The default value for this parameter. For constant parameters (readonlyValue=true), this is the fixed value. For editable parameters, this is the pre-filled default.

schema:readonlyValue.description: true = constant, fixed for every session (read-only in form). false = editable (default or optional depending on valueRequired).

schema:valueRequired.description: true = must be provided (mandatory). false = optional. Combined with readonlyValue: readonly+required = constant mandatory; !readonly+required = editable mandatory; !readonly+!required = optional.

schema:minValue.description: Minimum allowed numeric value. Defines the lower bound of a valid range at the method level; specific values within this range may be set per element in ada:targetSpeciesTemplate.

schema:maxValue.description: Maximum allowed numeric value. Upper bound of valid range.

schema:stepValue.description: Granularity expected of the value (e.g. 0.1 for nA).

schema:valuePattern.description: Regex pattern for validating string values.

schema:multipleValues.description: Whether multiple values are allowed (default false).

ada:fieldScope.description: Whether this parameter is fixed at the method level, varies per analytical session, or is element-specific.

ada:category.description: Grouping label for form layout (e.g. "Beam Conditions", "Data Processing", "Quality Control"). String for simple cases; DefinedTerm to link to a controlled vocabulary of parameter categories.

ada:dataType.description: Expected data type for the parameter value.

schema:unitCode.description: URI for unit of measure (QUDT preferred).

ada:cdifPropertyPath.description: The CDIF building block property path this parameter maps to. Used for JSON-LD serialisation.

ada:tier.description: Mandatory / Recommended / Optional tier from the metadata profile. Informs validation strictness.

MethodParameterValue.description: A read-only method parameter carrying the fixed protocol value, typed as schema:PropertyValue. Used for Advanced-protocol parameters that the analyst cannot change (the value is set by the protocol). The value is in schema:value; the human-readable label is in schema:name. Contrast with MethodParameter (schema:PropertyValueSpecification), used for editable parameters.

schema:propertyID.description: URI identifying this parameter type in a formal vocabulary. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}).

schema:value.description: The fixed protocol value for this read-only parameter.

KeyedTableColumn.description: Definition of one column of a KEYED TABLE, typed as schema:PropertyValueSpecification. A keyed table has one row per member of some domain -- a target species, a reported property, a monitored property -- and one column per field whose value repeats over that domain (the TAPP workbook's `Keyed By` column). Rows become schema:variableMeasured entries; columns become schema:additionalProperty within each. TargetSpeciesColumn and ReportedPropertyColumn are the two domains modelled so far; both are this shape.

schema:propertyID.description: URI identifying this column's parameter type in a formal vocabulary. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}).

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description:
Controlled vocabulary providing allowed values for this column. Four shapes are accepted: (1) a plain URI string identifying an external SKOS ConceptScheme; (2) an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere; (3) a LabeledLink (LinkRole with name and URL); (4) an inline schema:DefinedTermSet enumerating the allowed values
    as schema:DefinedTerm objects (replaces the prior ada:enumeration).

anyOf.description: Object reference to a vocabulary defined elsewhere.
Inline schema:DefinedTermSet listing the allowed values as schema:DefinedTerm objects. Use when no external vocabulary URI is available; replaces the deprecated ada:enumeration property.

schema:defaultValue.description: Default value for this column (pre-filled per row).

schema:readonlyValue.description: true = constant across all target species (read-only column).

schema:valueRequired.description: true = must be provided for every target-species row.

ada:cdifPropertyPath.description: How this column maps into the variableMeasured JSON-LD structure.

TargetSpeciesColumn.description: One column of the per-target-species parameter table. Structurally a KeyedTableColumn; kept as its own name because generated schemas and the shared targetSpeciesColumns registry $ref it.

TargetMaterialColumn.description: One column of the per-target-material parameter table. Structurally a KeyedTableColumn; kept as its own name because generated schemas and the shared targetMaterialColumns registry $ref it.

ReportedPropertyColumn.description: One column of the reported-property table. The reported properties are what the procedure REPORTS -- '206Pb/238U date (Ma)', 'd56Fe (permil vs IRMM-014)' -- as distinct from the target species and monitored properties it ACQUIRES. Structurally a KeyedTableColumn.

MonitoredPropertyColumn.description: One column of the monitored-property table. A monitored property is an instrument SELECTION POSITION -- a mass, a Faraday cup, an energy-loss edge, an X-ray line. It is not a flavour of target species: the target species is what is measured, the monitored property is the position it is measured on, and the two are independent. One target species may occupy several monitored properties, and MC-ICP-MS cups routinely monitor interferences that are not target species at all. Structurally a KeyedTableColumn.

MonitoredPropertyIdentifierColumn.description: The mandatory monitored-property-identifier column, naming the selection position in each row. Mirrors TargetSpeciesIdentifierColumn and ReportedPropertyIdentifierColumn; like both it maps into schema:variableMeasured/schema:name, because the variable list is shared across a procedure's table parts rather than owned by any one of them.

ReportedPropertyIdentifierColumn.description: The mandatory reported-property identifier column, naming the reported variable in each row. Mirrors TargetSpeciesIdentifierColumn: pinned constants fix the column's role as a row identifier rather than an editable parameter. Both identifier columns map into schema:variableMeasured/schema:name because the variable list is SHARED -- a procedure yields several tables (target species, monitored property, reported property) over one logical variable registry, not one table per document.

TargetMaterialIdentifierColumn.description: The mandatory target-material-identifier column, naming the material type in each row. Mirrors TargetSpeciesIdentifierColumn and MonitoredPropertyIdentifierColumn; like both it maps into schema:variableMeasured/schema:name, because the material a sampling unit hit is recorded as a column of the data table -- the variable list is shared across a procedure's table parts rather than owned by any one of them.

TargetSpeciesIdentifierColumn.description: The mandatory target-species-identifier column. Each row in the species table must carry a value for this column naming the analyzed constituent (e.g. "SiO2", "Fe"). Pinned constants enforce the column's role: readonly (the identifier of a row, not an editable parameter), required, mandatory tier, and a fixed mapping into schema:variableMeasured/schema:name. Long-term the value space should be a DefinedTermSet; for now a string.

ComputationalTool.description: Software application used for data acquisition, reduction, or processing. Follows Bioschemas ComputationalTool pattern.

schema:name.description: Name of the software (e.g. "Probe for EPMA").

schema:description.description: Role or purpose of this tool in the method.

schema:url.description: URL to the software product or documentation.

ada:toolRole.description: Role this software plays in the analytical workflow.

Reagent.description: A reference material, calibration standard, or chemical reagent. Follows Bioschemas reagent pattern with extensions for geochemistry reference materials.

@type.description: What the material IS, independent of the role it plays here (that is ada:reagentRole). One of the three kinds must be present: schema:DefinedTerm for a material identified by a registry entry (GeoReM, NIST SRM, USGS); schema:Product for a specific catalogued specimen or purchased lot (Smithsonian NMNH number, IGSN, in-house standard); schema:ChemicalSubstance for a bulk chemical or coating stock.

schema:name.description: Name of the material (e.g. "San Carlos olivine").

schema:identifier.description: Formal identifier (IGSN, catalog number, GeoReM ID).

schema:termCode.description: Registry code for the material on the schema:DefinedTerm path (e.g. "SRM 610", "ATHO-G").

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description: The registry the schema:termCode belongs to (GeoReM, NIST SRM catalogue, USGS RM list).

ada:reagentRole.description: Role of this material in the method.

schema:citation.description: Publication reference for the standard's accepted values.

PropertyIDValue.description:
One value of schema:propertyID: a vocabulary URI, a JSON-LD IRI reference, or a DefinedTerm.
Whether the property holding these is an ARRAY depends on which job schema:PropertyValue is doing, because schema.org overloads that one class for several things that ought to be distinct (see the CDIF Core Implementation Guide, "Polymorphism of PropertyValue"):

  * schema:additionalProperty and schema:variableMeasured -- a measured or declared parameter.
    propertyID is 0..* there, so it is ALWAYS an array and a consumer iterates without first
    testing the value's type.
  * schema:identifier -- an identifier for the identifier scheme (DOI, ARK, IGSN). Upstream
    types that one as a bare string or {"@id": ...}, never an array, so do NOT wrap it.

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.id.description:
Properties for a schema.org identifier (schema:PropertyValue pattern).
**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:Identifier / schema:PropertyValue is represented by a single attribute
of that class type. The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value
to be EITHER a plain string (interpreted as the bare identifier value) OR a
full schema:PropertyValue object (with explicit @type, propertyID, value).
Consumers should accept either form.

schema:propertyID.description: In this context for the schema:PropertyValue, this field is an identifier for the identifier schema, e.g. DOI, ARK.  Get values from https://registry.identifiers.org/registry/ for interoperability. URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}) so they participate in RDF entailment; free-label strings remain valid as strings.

schema:url.description: web-resolveable string for the identifier; host name part is location of a resolver that will return some representation for the given identifier value. E.g. https://doi.org/10.5066/F7VX0DMQ

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.de.description:
schema.org Defined Term schema.

**Union-type policy:** In CDIF profile UML models an attribute typed as
schema:DefinedTerm is represented by a single attribute of that class type.
The JSON Schema implementation permits the property value to be EITHER a
plain string (interpreted as schema:name or schema:termCode in the default
vocabulary) OR a full schema:DefinedTerm object (with explicit @type, name,
identifier, termCode, inDefinedTermSet). Consumers should accept either form.

Note that this differs from the cdif Concept policy: a Concept (skos:Concept)
in CDIF profiles MUST be a controlled-vocabulary entry (object form or
@id-reference) — plain strings are not permitted for Concept-typed values
because vocabulary identity cannot be recovered from an unscoped label.

schema:name.description: text label for the term that is useful to human user

schema:inDefinedTermSet.description: The controlled vocabulary responsible for this keyword, as EITHER a plain URI string identifying the vocabulary, OR an object reference ({"@id": "<uri>"}) to a vocabulary defined elsewhere in the document. Both forms are already in use across CDIF profiles and downstream ADA building blocks; permitting only the string form made the object form - the natural JSON-LD spelling of a reference - invalid, while this class's own union-type policy above explicitly anticipates both.

schema:termCode.description: A representative code for this keyword in the controlled vocabulary. Analogous to skos:Notation

ogch.BaseSchema.instrument.title: ADA Analysis Instrument
ogch.BaseSchema.instrument.description: ADA analytical instrument building block. Extends the core CDIF instrument building block with NeXus NXinstrument classification via additionalType. Instruments are typed as schema:Thing + schema:Product (from core) with domain-specific types (e.g. nxs:base_classes/NXinstrument.html, ada:AMSInstrument) in additionalType.

@id.description: Identifier for this instrument within the record. REQUIRED: an instrument has to be referenceable. A monitored species names the instrument (or the instrument part) that reports it, and a dataset variable points back at the device that produced it; neither is expressible while the instrument is an anonymous object. A document-scoped identifier suffices, but a resolvable one is better wherever the lab has a persistent identifier for the device.

schema:additionalType.description: Domain-specific instrument type classifications. Should include a NeXus base class (e.g. nxs:base_classes/NXinstrument.html) and/or technique-specific identifier (e.g. ada:AMSInstrument, GCMD instrument identifier). URI-shape values MUST be serialized as JSON-LD IRI references ({"@id":"..."}); free-label strings remain valid. Every instrument additionally carries the Wikidata "measuring instrument" type, which is invariant across techniques: the technique-specific entry says what KIND of instrument this is and varies by profile, while the Wikidata term says that it is an instrument at all, and gives a consumer one term to select on without knowing the ADA vocabulary.

schema:hasPart.description: Sub-components of this instrument system (a torch, an ICP source, a collision/reaction cell, a spectrometer). A component IS an instrument -- same @type (schema:Product + schema:Thing), same Wikidata term, and its own schema:additionalType token saying which kind of component it is. The shape is restated rather than written as `$ref: '#'`, because resolve_schema replaces a circular ref with an empty stub -- it would read as "a part is an instrument" and enforce nothing. Upstream types a component more loosely (schema:Thing alone, no Wikidata); this narrows it, and the two compose because allOf intersects.

@id.description: Identifier for this component within the record. REQUIRED on an INLINE component for the same reason it is required on the instrument: a monitored species names the part that reports it -- a Faraday cup, a spectrometer, a detector -- and an anonymous object cannot be referenced. The sibling branch of this anyOf is the by-reference form, a bare {"@id": ...} pointing at a component described elsewhere.

ada:collectorConfiguration.description: How masses are assigned to collector positions for this procedure, AS THE SOURCE STATES IT. Free text on purpose: submitters write this as prose or as a semicolon-separated list in no agreed syntax ("L3=116Sn (Sn); L2=117Sn (Sn); Ax=120Sn ..."), and in many cases it cannot be parsed at all. Recording the statement verbatim is what can always be done; ada:collectors below is what can sometimes be done as well. Meaningful on a component whose schema:additionalType includes 'Collector'.

ada:collectors.description:
The collector table. One member per position when ada:collectorConfiguration parses into positions, and ONE member carrying the text as written when it does not -- the N=1 form of the flattening fallback that TAPP-keyed-values-design.md Decision 6 settles for every keyed axis: "rather than admit two shapes, always emit the table: a declaration that does not parse into members yields a one-row table whose row key is the text as written. The fallback is then not a separate branch but N=1."
So a consumer reads one shape either way. In the N=1 form schema:name is a fixed label rather than a cup ('Collector configuration description'), schema:description carries the unparsed string, and the per-item values ride in schema:additionalProperty as name/value pairs. Parsing these strings to individual collectors is not tractable in general -- they are written for a person to read -- so N=1 is expected to be the common case, not the exception.
This exists because a cup label has to be referenceable WHEN there is one. A per-cup quantity (a baseline, a gain factor) and a monitored property that names the position reporting it both need something to point AT, and a label buried in a sentence is not something a consumer can join to. schema:name is that anchor.
What a collector does NOT carry is which monitored property it measures. That assignment is procedure configuration, not hardware -- the same physical array is wired differently by another procedure, and an analysis may override it -- so it lives as the 'collector' column of ada:monitoredPropertyColumns on the method definition, whose values are these schema:names. Putting it here would invert the dependency and make the instrument description procedure-specific.
Note what an N=1 member does NOT assert: it names no cup, so it makes no per-cup claim. That matters because the resistor values are attested per MASS, not per cup (Proposal_Monitored_Property_2026-09-10 §10), and the fallback must not quietly move them onto the collector axis.

schema:name.description: The collector position label as the instrument names it -- L5..L1, C or Ax, H1..H5, IC1..IC8 on a Neptune-class multicollector. This is the identifier other properties reference. In the N=1 fallback there is no position to name, so it is the fixed label 'Collector configuration description' and nothing should join to it.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Quantities carried on this member as name/value pairs. In the parsed form these are per-position quantities that cannot be restated per mass -- a baseline, a gain factor. In the N=1 form they are the source fields themselves, each as its item name and the text as written, which is how an unparseable per-collector statement is preserved without inventing an assignment it does not make.

schema:name.description: The item name, e.g. 'Faraday Cup Amplifier Resistor Values'.

schema:value.description: The value, as written when it did not parse.

anyOf.description: Reference by node @id to a component described elsewhere.

ogch.BaseSchema.laboratory.title: ADA Analysis Laboratory
ogch.BaseSchema.laboratory.description: ADA laboratory or facility building block. Extends the core CDIF spatialExtent (schema:Place) with NeXus NXsource classification via additionalType. Inherits place name, identifier, alternateName, geo coordinates, and geosparql geometry from spatialExtent.

schema:additionalType.description: Must classify the place as a NeXus NXsource. The value is a sealed reference ({"@id": ...}) so JSON-LD expands it to a real IRI; written as a bare string it stays a literal that looks like a URI and resolves to nothing. The two-segment path is the form that actually resolves -- .../classes/BaseClass/NXsource is a 404, .../classes/base_classes/NXsource.html is not.

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.pe.description: schema for cdif profile of schema.org/Person

schema:name.description: string label for person that is meaningful for human users, should format consistently. Recommend 'Family Name, Given name' format.

schema:description.description: additional information about the agent or their relation to the described resource

schema:alternateName.description: other labels by which the person might be known

schema:affiliation.description: if affiliation is present, value must be a schema:Organization.

schema:contactPoint.description: restrict to email only. Schema.org allows telephone and postal contacts as well

schema:name.description: string label for organization that is meaningful for human users

schema:alternateName.description: other labels by which the organization might be known

schema:description.description: additional information about the agent or their relation to the described resource

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.la.description:
Schema for a labeled link, a profile of schema.org/CreativeWork: a resolvable URL with an optional name and description. Optionally carries the DCAT relation surface (dcat:hadRole, dcterms:relation) for a link that expresses a typed relationship rather than a plain reference.
Those two properties were a separate block, cdifDataType/cdifReference, which was an allOf of this schema plus exactly those two optional properties and nothing else -- its dcat:Relationship co-type mandate had already been removed because it made every labeled link unsatisfiable and broke every schema:license example that followed schema.org's own advice. Since both are optional, folding them in here changes no document's validity while removing a block and five levels of $defs/Reference indirection. cdifReference was retired 2026-09-23.

@type.description:
Either construct, or both. A labeled link is a schema:CreativeWork at a URL; a dcat:Relationship is DCAT's association class for a typed relation to another resource. A node may declare both -- CDIF's own relation examples do -- but NEITHER IS REQUIRED TO ACCOMPANY THE OTHER.
That is the whole point of the anyOf. Until 2026-09-08 this block's Relation half required contains: dcat:Relationship while the labeled-link half required contains: schema:CreativeWork, and under allOf both applied to every instance, so an ordinary labeled link was unsatisfiable. Of profile-core's licenses the 29 plain strings and 1 @id-reference passed while the 10 that followed schema.org's own recommendation -- "use schema:CreativeWork to provide a label (name) for the license" -- failed. 412782113 fixed that by deleting the dcat:Relationship mandate outright, which left the JSON Schema with no notion of dcat:Relationship at all while rules.shacl went on targeting it as a class. A pure DCAT relation then met a SHACL requirement with no schema counterpart. This anyOf restores the type to the schema WITHOUT restoring the conjunction.

dcat:hadRole.description:
Role of the related resource. Present only on a link that expresses a relationship; a plain labeled link such as a license omits it.
DCAT's declared range is dcat:Role (dcat.ttl: rdfs:range dcat:Role, and dcat:Role rdfs:subClassOf skos:Concept), so the DCAT-native form is a node typed dcat:Role. That form was NOT accepted here before 2026-10-01: this property was cdifConceptOrTermOrString alone, which matches a bare string, a sealed @id reference, a schema:DefinedTerm or a skos:Concept -- none of which a dcat:Role-typed node satisfies, because JSON Schema does no subclass reasoning.
dcat:Role is added as a branch rather than replacing the others, so the DCAT-native form becomes valid without invalidating anything already written. Note this leaves CDIF LOOSER than DCAT, deliberately: DCAT's range is dcat:Role alone, and CDIF also accepts a plain skos:Concept, a DefinedTerm, an @id reference and a string. That is the same both-forms stance taken on dcterms:relation, and it is a choice rather than an oversight -- do not read the extra branches as something not yet tightened.

dcterms:relation.description:
The related resource -- the DCAT canonical pointer to what is being related to, which is distinct from schema:url, the presentation URL of the link itself.
An @id reference is the RECOMMENDED form and a string is permitted, which is DCMI's own position: "Recommended practice is to identify the related resource by means of a URI. If this is not possible or feasible, a string conforming to a formal identification system may be provided." DCMI declares no rdfs:range for this property, and of the 13 DCMI properties carrying an "intended to be used with non-literal values" restriction, this is deliberately not one. dcat.ttl does not re-declare or constrain it at all -- the only triple mentioning it in the whole DCAT vocabulary is `dcat:distribution rdfs:subPropertyOf dcterms:relation`.
So objectReference-only would be stricter than both DCAT and DCMI and would reject a form the specification sanctions. The anyOf matches how schema:additionalType is handled here: both forms valid, the object form used in examples and required only where a `contains` pins a specific value.
It was string-only until 2026-10-01, which rejected the @id form outright. Reported from outside by a PSDI validator taking a things-not-strings approach (profile-core#16): their DCAT catalogue mirrors the DCAT-3 spec examples and wrote {"@id": ...}, which failed both layers -- while CDIF's own documented URI serialization policy (agents.md) says URI values SHOULD be {"@id": ...}. The register required the one form its own policy argues against.

DcatRole.description:
A dcat:Role -- DCAT's declared range for dcat:hadRole. Defined inline rather than as its own building block because nothing else in the register needs it yet; dcat:hadRole's domain is owl:unionOf [prov:Attribution, dcat:Relationship], so promote it to a block if a qualified attribution ever needs the same shape.
dcat:Role rdfs:subClassOf skos:Concept, so the skos:prefLabel / skos:inScheme furniture of a concept is permitted alongside; it is not required here because DCAT states no cardinality constraints on the class -- dcat.ttl declares no rdfs:subClassOf and no owl:Restriction on dcat:Relationship, and the "mandatory" wording in the DCAT-3 document is prose in the spec tables rather than an axiom in the vocabulary.

@id.description: IRI of the role concept, ideally from a controlled vocabulary.

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.mo.description: Funding acknowledgement properties, profile of schema.org/MonetaryGrant

@id.description: URI identifier for this funding record

schema:description.description: description of the funding or grant

@id.description: a identifier for an agent defined in this metadata, or externally; must be dereferenceable

cdif.bbr.metadata.qualityProperties.qual.title: definitions for simple quality measure property

dqv:isMeasurementOf.description: specify the quality measure that is reported, by name, with an ID ref, or as a Defined Term

@id.description: a resolvable reference to a representation of a quality measure

dqv:value.description: the reported result of the quality measure, as a string, a number, or a defined term from a vocabulary

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.in.title: Instrument Description
cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.in.description: Schema for describing laboratory instruments and instrument systems. Supports ownership, manufacturer, model, commissioning dates, hierarchical sub-components via schema:hasPart, and domain-specific typing. Instruments may be standalone devices or complex systems with sub-components.

@id.description: Persistent identifier URI for this instrument metadata record.

@type.description: Must include schema:Product and schema:Thing. May include additional types.

schema:additionalType.description: Domain-specific type classifications. Should include a scientific instrument type URI (e.g. wd:Q3099911 for Wikidata scientific instrument).

schema:description.description: Text description of this instrument, its purpose, and capabilities.

schema:alternateName.description: Alternate name(s), e.g. specific make/model designation, common abbreviation.

schema:identifier.description: Formal identifier(s) for this instrument. Use PropertyValue for structured identifiers (e.g. PIDINST, serial number, inventory number).

schema:url.description: Landing page URL for this instrument.

schema:model.description: Product model information for this instrument.

schema:category.description: Instrument type classification(s) from a controlled vocabulary.

schema:contributor.description: Agents associated with this instrument in specific roles (e.g. operator, custodian, principal investigator). Use schema:owner for the owning organization.

schema:additionalProperty.description: Instrument-specific properties (measured variables, detection limits, calibration information, operating parameters, etc.). On a procedure / plan instrument (e.g. an instrument named directly on an ada:TAPPDefinition) these are schema:PropertyValueSpecification parameter templates (an overridable default); on a prov:used analysis-event instrument they are schema:PropertyValue concrete values. The JSON Schema accepts both; a profile SHACL rule pins which form applies in which context.

schema:validThrough.description: Date the instrument was decommissioned (ISO 8601). Absent if still operational.

schema:hasPart.description: Sub-components of this instrument system. Each item is either an inline instrument description or an @id reference.

@id.description: Reference to a sub-component defined elsewhere.

schema:relatedLink.description: Links to related resources (manuals, datasheets, calibration records, related instruments), each naming how the target relates to the instrument. Uses the same linkRole block as cdifCore; before 2026-09-23 this property was a labeled link here and a LinkRole there.

schema:subjectOf.description: Catalog record metadata-about-metadata for this instrument description.

schema:dateModified.description: Date this metadata record was last modified (ISO 8601).

dcterms:conformsTo.description: Schema or profile this metadata record conforms to.

AdditionalPropertySpecification.title: additionalProperty PropertyValueSpecification
AdditionalPropertySpecification.description:
A parameter specification (an overridable default) declared on a procedure / plan instrument, typed schema:PropertyValueSpecification; the default sits in schema:defaultValue. Contrast with AdditionalProperty (schema:PropertyValue), the concrete-value form carried by a prov:used analysis-event instrument.
Until 2026-10-09 this declared only '@type' and schema:name, so the description named schema:defaultValue as the point of the shape while the schema did not declare it. The object is open, so nothing failed -- 203 entries in geochemBuildingBlocks carried a default that no schema described, and a placement path ending in schema:defaultValue could not be told from a misspelling.
A domain profile adds its own keys here (geochemBuildingBlocks carries ada:dataType and ada:fieldScope on every one of these entries). Those stay out of this block: it is a generic schema.org shape with several consumers, and only the schema.org properties are its to declare.

schema:valueName.description: Machine-readable name for the parameter, for serialization and for binding a form control to it.

schema:defaultValue.description: The overridable default this specification carries -- the value that applies unless the analysis overrides it. Left untyped: a default may be a string, a number or a boolean, and which one is a property of the parameter rather than of this shape.

schema:value.description: A value fixed by the procedure, where the parameter is NOT overridable. Both keys are declared because both occur: measured across the geochemBuildingBlocks corpus on 2026-10-09, of 369 PropertyValueSpecification entries under schema:instrument, 203 carry schema:defaultValue and 166 carry schema:value. A specification that pins a value rather than defaulting one is still a specification.

schema:description.description: Guidance text for the parameter, e.g. shown beside a form control.

@id.description: Identifier for this specification, so a recorded value elsewhere can reference the parameter it instantiates.

InstrumentComponent.description: A sub-component of an instrument system. Uses the same structure as the parent instrument but without nesting (single level of hasPart).

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.sp.description: Spatial Extent description for CDIF discovery profile.  Note required prefix declaration for geoSparql ( http://www.opengis.net/ont/geosparql#) and OGC simple features (sf: http://www.opengis.net/ont/sf#)

schema:additionalType.description: Domain-specific type classifications for this place (e.g. facility type,laboratory classification, feature type).

schema:name.description: A place name for the location, either as a string or a DefinedTerm from a gazetteer.

schema:identifier.description: Formal identifier for this place (e.g. ROR identifier for a facility).

schema:alternateName.description: Alternate or abbreviated name(s) for this place.

schema:geo.description: Either a bounding box or a point location.

anyOf.description: A point location. Point locations are recommended for data that is associated with specific sample locations, particularly if these are widely spaced such that an enclosing bounding box would be a misleading representation of the spatial location. Be aware that some client applications might only index or display bounding box extents or a single point location.

A schema:GeoShape bounding box. The geometry is described with a set of latitude/longitude pairs (in that order).The documentation for schema:GeoShape states 'Either whitespace or commas can be used to separate latitude and longitude; whitespace should be used when writing a list of several such points.'

schema:box.description: A GeoShape box defines an area on the surface of the earth defined by point locations of the southwest corner and northeast corner of the rectangle in latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The two corner coordinate points are separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian.

anyOf.description: A schema:GeoShape curvilinear trace, for resource related to a linear trace like a ship track or airplane flight line

schema:line.description: A GeoShape box defines a curvilinear geometry as a string of latitude-longitude coordinates. A space should be used to separate the latitude and longitude values. The coordinate point pairs are also separated by a space. 'East longitude' means positive longitude values are east of the prime (Greenwich) meridian. e.g. '39.33 120.77 40.44 123.96 41.00 121.34'

geosparql:hasGeometry.description: Optional geographic extent using wkt geometry, see Ocean InfoHub (https://book.oceaninfohub.org/thematics/spatial/README.html#simple-geosparql-wkt). Other geometry schemes might be specified in a specific domain profile, e.g. for atmospheric, subsurface data, or local coordinate systems. NOTE that the location specified here should be the same as the schema.org point or contained within the specified bounding box.

@type.description: MUST be sf: (<http://www.opengis.net/ont/sf#>) SimpleFeature geometry type. See https://opengeospatial.github.io/ogc-geosparql/geosparql11/sf_geometries.ttl

@value.description: a WKT geometry description string, e.g. 'POINT(-76 -18)'

@id.description: identifier string for coordinate reference system, e.g., 'CRS84'

cdif.bbr.metadata.cdifDataType.cdifConce.title: CDIF Concept-or-Term-or-String
cdif.bbr.metadata.cdifDataType.cdifConce.description: Shared shape for a CDIF property that carries either a controlled-vocabulary value or a bare string label. Wraps cdifConceptOrTerm (SKOS-concept @id-ref, schema:DefinedTerm, or inline cdif:Concept) with a plain-string alternative used for legacy or single-word labels not yet bound to a vocabulary.

cdif.bbr.metadata.cdifDataType.objectRef.title: Object Reference
cdif.bbr.metadata.cdifDataType.objectRef.description: A reference to a node defined elsewhere, by its @id.

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.ag.description: For more granularity on how a person contributed to a Dataset, use schema:Role. The schema.org documentation does not state that the Role type is an expected data type of author, creator and contributor, but that is addressed in this blog post (http://blog.schema.org/2014/06/introducing-role.html). see https://github.com/ESIPFed/science-on-schema.org/blob/develop/guides/Dataset.md#roles-of-people

@id.description: IRI reference to a Person or Organization defined elsewhere

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.ad.title: additionalProperty PropertyValue
cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.ad.description: PropertyValue values required to define a soft-typed property with a value.

schema:propertyID.description: identifier or name for the property concept quantified by the values in this variable slot. Multiple values can specify the property at different levels of granularity.

cdif.bbr.metadata.schemaorgProperties.li.description:
A typed link, implemented as a schema.org LinkRole: schema:linkRelationship names how the target relates to the subject, and schema:target carries the EntryPoint actually being linked to.
This is the right shape when the relationship itself is the point -- "this is the canonical version of", "this is the download endpoint for". Where the value is simply a work at a URL, such as a license or a terms-of-service document, use schemaorgProperties/labeledLink instead: a licence is a work, not a role, and wrapping it in a Role forces every consumer through an indirection to reach the thing itself.
Defined here as a block rather than inline in a profile (where it lived until 2026-09-23) so that more than one consumer can reuse it. While it was inline in cdifCore, schemaorgProperties/instrument could not reach it and defined schema:relatedLink as a labeled link instead -- the same property carrying two different shapes depending on which node held it.

schema:linkRelationship.description: How the target relates to the subject, as a controlled-vocabulary value or a plain string label. Required: a typed link whose relationship is unstated carries no more information than a bare URL, which is what schemaorgProperties/labeledLink is for.

schema:target.description: The entry point being linked to. Deliberately not sealed: real targets also carry schema:httpMethod, schema:urlTemplate, schema:contentType and domain-specific properties, and JSON-LD is open-world.

cdif.bbr.metadata.cdifDataType.cdifConce.description: A SKOS concept identified by URI, a schema:DefinedTerm, or an inline cdif:Concept. Shared shape used wherever a CDIF property carries either a controlled-vocabulary reference or an inline concept definition.

anyOf.description: reference to a skos concept for the data type

cdif.bbr.metadata.skosProperties.skosCon.title: SKOS Concept
cdif.bbr.metadata.skosProperties.skosCon.description: JSON Schema for a SKOS Concept in JSON-LD form. A unit of thought within a concept scheme. Supports labels (prefLabel, altLabel, hiddenLabel), notations, hierarchical relations (broader/narrower), associative relations (related), cross-scheme mapping properties, scheme membership, and documentary notes. Based on the W3C SKOS Reference (https://www.w3.org/TR/skos-reference/).

@context.description: JSON-LD context declaring the skos namespace prefix. May be a single object or an array of strings and objects.

skos:prefLabel.description: Preferred lexical label for this concept. A single string, a single language-tagged value, or an array of language-tagged values. Each language should appear at most once.

skos:notation.description: Classification code for this concept within a scheme (a single notation string, consistent with CdifCodelistConcept).

skos:definition.description: Formal explanation of the meaning of this concept.

skos:scopeNote.description: Note clarifying meaning and/or intended use.

skos:historyNote.description: Note about past state or use.

skos:inScheme.description: Concept scheme(s) this concept belongs to.

skos:topConceptOf.description: Concept scheme(s) for which this is a top concept.

skos:broader.description: Broader (parent) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

skos:narrower.description: Narrower (child) concepts in the hierarchy. Items are inline concept objects or @id references.

ConceptRef.description: A reference to a SKOS Concept by URI.

LanguageTaggedValue.description: An RDF literal value with a language tag, serialized as a JSON-LD value object.

@language.description: BCP 47 language tag (e.g. en, fr, de).

title: TAPP Composition Module: UPb
description:
The shared UPb block of the 2026-08-11 TAPP library (Claude Skills for TAPP/Module_UPb.csv), composed by 3 of the sixteen delivery tables. 3 owned fields over 1 schema paths.

GENERATED by tools/build_module_bb.py from the module's CSV and its schema-path sidecar — edit those, not this file. Requiredness follows the TAPP tier matrix: a field Basic on a side is required there, Advanced is permitted, N/A is absent from that side entirely.

This is a PROFILE, not a vocabulary: it asserts which properties a conforming procedure or analysis carries. Column F (Example / Allowed Content) is consumer-owned per the module manifest, so no enum is pinned here — a consuming TAPP may narrow a value space, never widen it.

ProcedureIdentification.title: UPb on the procedure
ProcedureIdentification.description: Composed into a TAPP (prov:Plan) schema: what the procedure asserts once, for every analysis that follows it.

ada:chemicalAbrasionConditions.description: Annealing and partial-dissolution conditions applied to mitigate Pb loss before analysis, following Mattinson (2005): annealing temperature and duration, and the acid, temperature and duration of the partial-dissolution step. Record 'None' where grains were analysed untreated.

Param_Procedure_intermediateDaughterDise.title: Intermediate Daughter Disequilibrium Correction
Param_Procedure_intermediateDaughterDise.description: Correction for initial disequilibrium in intermediate daughter products of the U decay chains — principally 230Th, and where relevant 231Pa — together with the Th/U or Pa/U partitioning value assumed and its source. Record 'None' with a justification where no correction was applied.

Param_Procedure_discordanceDefinitionAnd.title: Discordance Definition and Values
Param_Procedure_discordanceDefinitionAnd.description: How discordance between the 206Pb/238U, 207Pb/235U and 207Pb/206Pb chronometers is defined for this procedure, and the discordance values obtained. State the formula used. The rule for excluding discordant analyses, and how many were excluded, belong in Analysis Inclusion and Rejection Criteria.
